home.aboutTitle: Nice to meet you, I'm Karl
about: I'm a dog trainer and I work with families, couples, puppies and adult dogs of every size. I believe a dog that understands what is expected of it is a calmer dog, and owners who understand their dog enjoy it much more.
My training is based on consistency, patience and positive reinforcement. In the first meeting I get to know the dog and the home, and build a plan that fits the dog, the family and your routine.
I've worked with dogs that pulled on the leash, barked at every passer-by, were afraid of noises or couldn't stay home alone. In most cases the change starts within the first few weeks.

services.title: My services
services.intro: Tap a service to see what it includes and who it's for. Not sure what fits? Start with a consultation visit.

items.title: Consultation and assessment
items.short: Getting to know your dog, understanding what's going on and building a plan.
items.body: A visit of about an hour and a half at your home. I watch the dog in its natural environment, hear from you what bothers you and what your goals are, and explain the right way forward.

items.title: Puppy training
items.short: The right start from day one at home.
items.body: Puppies learn fast, and this is the time to build good habits. We'll work on toilet training, play biting, sleeping through the night, getting used to the leash and meeting the world.
includes: First steps on the leash and first commands
A socialization plan for people, dogs and noises

items.title: Basic obedience
items.short: Leash walking, sit, down, stay and come.
items.body: The basics every dog needs to live calmly with the family and in the city. Training takes place at your home or as board and train, and every program ends with a handover session where I teach you the commands.
includes: Calm behavior at home and when guests arrive
A handover session with the family

items.title: Advanced obedience
items.short: Full control, off the leash and in busy places.
items.body: For dogs that already know the basics. We'll strengthen commands at a distance, with distractions and in busy places, and work on heel and off-leash work.
includes: Commands at a distance and with distractions
Behavior in cafés and busy places
A handover session and follow-up practice

items.title: Behavior problems
items.short: Barking, aggression, fears, separation anxiety and pulling.
items.body: Behavior problems don't go away on their own. I find the cause, not just the symptom, and build a gradual plan with you that fits the dog and the home.
includes: Finding the source of the problem

items.title: Help choosing the right dog
items.short: Before you adopt or buy, choose well.
items.body: Breed, size, energy level and temperament should fit your home and routine. I help you understand what fits, and I can also join you to meet the dog before you decide.
includes: A matching call based on your lifestyle

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: Tap a question to see the answer. Didn't find yours? Send me a message.

items.q: Why train a dog at all, and from what age can you start?
items.a: Training strengthens your dog's understanding and builds an emotional bond between you and your four-legged friend. Training can start from 4 months old, and puppy education can start from the moment you bring your dog home.

items.q: How do I get my dog to stop pulling and barking at everyone we pass?
items.a: Barking and pulling are your dog's way of communicating fear, alertness or excitement. In our work we won't "silence" the dog. We'll help it change its emotional response to what happens outside, and give it a sense of security by your side.

items.q: Is training based on punishment or on treats?
items.a: The work focuses on building cooperation that comes from the dog's own will and motivation, using positive reinforcement and an understanding of its needs, to build a strong, healthy bond that prevents behavior problems in advance.

items.q: I'm busy and don't have much free time during the week. Can I still start and succeed?
items.a: Absolutely. The goal is to fit the tools into your natural daily routine. Even 10 to 15 minutes of focused practice during your regular daily walk can make a real change in your dog's behavior.

items.q: I adopted an adult dog. Can its habits still change, or is it too late?
items.a: You can always teach a dog new things, at any age. Training an adult dog takes a suitable pace, and it's one of the best ways to build trust, boundaries and a shared language in its new home.
